correctness.rationale: The rational-independence premise is published and its proof is examined; the fixed-lag product follows by two-arc geometry and a rigorously bounded infinite-ray tail. A second finite-dimensional Kronecker argument with uniform product tails proves convergence of the lag-empirical law. Compact connectedness, conditioning on the earliest positive overlap, and integral identities give the interval support, unique atom, absolutely continuous remainder and strictly positive variance. The self-contained checker independently corroborates exact ray membership and finite-product predictions for eight k=2 rays, 500,000 windows and seven lags; it is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The arithmetic mixing question for intervals devoid of nonperfect-power k-full integers is natural from the recent statistics of h_k. The result completely describes the covariance values visited over arbitrarily long integer lags, including an interval of both signs, an atom with a precise geometric interpretation, an absolutely continuous complement and nonzero variance. These properties are not supplied by a one-window frequency or a single adjacent-window covariance.
